question: What is the main job of the mucosa, the innermost layer of your gut?

options.D: Anchoring the tract to the abdominal wall

explanation: You've got this! The mucosa faces right inside the tube, making it our body's frontline hero for soaking up nutrients and keeping things slippery with mucus. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which layer of the gut wall is directly responsible for pushing food forward with wave-like squeezes?
explanation: Great job! The muscularis externa has smooth muscle layers that team up to move food smoothly along the digestive tract. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is the name of the muscular food pipe that connects your throat to your stomach?
explanation: Spot on! The esophagus is our dedicated highway for swallowing food down from the throat to the stomach. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h2)

question: Why does the valve at the bottom of the esophagus close tightly after food enters the stomach?

options.A: To signal the brain that a meal has finished
options.B: To stop acidic stomach contents from flowing backward
options.C: To prevent air from entering the abdominal cavity
options.D: To trap food in the esophagus for further chewing

explanation: Spot on! This little muscular gatekeeper stops harsh stomach acid from splashing back up and burning the food pipe. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h2)

question: Special parietal cells in the stomach secrete a substance you need to absorb vitamin B12. What is it called?
explanation: You're doing great! Intrinsic factor acts like a VIP ticket for vitamin B12, helping the lower small intestine absorb it properly. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of the strong hydrochloric acid made in your stomach?

options.A: Breaking down dietary fats into fatty acids
options.B: Activating digestive enzymes and killing microbes
options.C: Protecting the stomach lining from mechanical wear
options.D: Absorbing water directly into the bloodstream

explanation: Well done! Stomach acid creates a tough shield that kills germs and turns inactive pepsinogen into working digestive enzymes. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h3)

question: What are the three parts of the small intestine in order, starting right after the stomach?
explanation: Easy to remember once you say it a few times: food flows from the stomach into the duodenum, then the jejunum, and finally the ileum! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h4)

question: How do tiny villi and microvilli help the small intestine do its job better?

options.A: By producing strong acid to break down tough plant fibers
options.B: By pushing waste products quickly toward the large bowel
options.C: By greatly increasing the surface area available for absorption
options.D: By storing excess water during times of dehydration

explanation: Brilliant! These tiny finger-like folds give the small intestine a massive surface area so it can soak up as many nutrients as possible. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the main job of bile, which is produced by the liver?
explanation: You've got this! Bile acts like dish soap for fats, breaking big blobs into tiny droplets so digestive enzymes can easily break them down. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why does the pancreas release bicarbonate into the small intestine?

options.A: To stimulate the liver to produce more cholesterol
options.B: To lubricate the intestinal walls for easier transit
options.C: To break down protein chains into individual amino acids
options.D: To neutralize the acidic chyme coming from the stomach

explanation: Spot on! Bicarbonate is alkaline, meaning it cools down and neutralizes the harsh acid coming from the stomach so it doesn't harm your gut lining. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h5)

question: What are the main jobs of the large intestine?

options.A: Producing bile and filtering toxins from the blood
options.B: Secreting hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor
options.C: Digesting proteins and absorbing simple sugars
options.D: Absorbing water and compacting indigestible waste

explanation: Well done! The large intestine mainly soaks up remaining water and turns leftover food into solid stool ready for elimination. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h6)

question: What helpful role do the resident bacteria in your colon play?

options.A: Digesting the majority of dietary fats and proteins
options.B: Producing protective mucus for the rectal lining
options.C: Synthesizing certain vitamins and fermenting fiber
options.D: Preventing all water absorption to keep stool soft

explanation: Correct! Our gut bacteria are friendly helpers that break down fiber and even manufacture important nutrients like vitamin K for us. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h6)

question: How would you best describe peristalsis?

options.A: Wave-like muscle contractions that push food forward
options.B: Localized churning that mixes food in the small intestine
options.C: The absorption of water through the large bowel wall
options.D: The secretion of digestive enzymes by the pancreas

explanation: Spot on! Think of peristalsis like a wave of muscle squeezes moving food steadily along down the digestive tube. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h7)

question: How is segmentation different from peristalsis in the gut?

options.A: Segmentation occurs only in the stomach while peristalsis is in the colon.
options.B: Segmentation mixes food back and forth rather than moving it forward.
options.C: Segmentation is controlled by the brain while peristalsis is automatic.
options.D: Segmentation stops all digestion while peristalsis speeds it up.

explanation: You're doing great! While peristalsis pushes food forward, segmentation uses ring-like squeezes to thoroughly blend food back and forth with digestive juices. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h7)

question: Which physical assessment step must a nurse ALWAYS do before pressing on a patient's abdomen?
explanation: Awesome clinical thinking! Always listen with your stethoscope first so you don't accidentally alter natural bowel sounds by pressing on the tummy. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h8)

question: A patient after surgery has a swollen tummy, has not passed gas, and you hear zero bowel sounds. What condition do you suspect?
explanation: Spot on! When the bowel temporarily goes to sleep and stops moving after surgery, we call it a paralytic ileus. Keep up the brilliant nursing instincts! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h8)
